paragraphs.source_en: These disquisitions reminded him of the answer he once got from a little boy whom he met coming home from school. Nekhludoff asked him if he had learned his spelling.

units.source_en: These disquisitions reminded him of the answer he once got from a little boy whom he met coming home from school.
Nekhludoff asked him if he had learned his spelling.

paragraphs.source_en: “Well, then, tell me, how do you spell ‘leg’?”

units.source_en: “Well, then, tell me, how do you spell ‘leg’?”

paragraphs.source_en: “A dog’s leg, or what kind of leg?” the boy answered, with a sly look.

paragraphs.source_en: Answers in the form of new questions, like the boy’s, was all Nekhludoff got in reply to his one primary question. He found much that was clever, learned much that was interesting, but what he did not find was an answer to the principal question: By what right some people punish others?
